summary: Traced the new configuration-history lead to a negative result and recorded the premise that carries it. The question was whether a follower could hold a committed configuration that was never committed and then truncate its log so that its latest configuration names a server with no entry behind it; the trace answers no for a leader using this library's configuration API, for two reasons. The leader's own gate (configurationChangeChIfStable) only returns the change channel while latestIndex equals committedIndex and the leader's commit index has reached the first entry of its term, so a configuration entry can only exist after the entry below it was committed — which is what makes processConfigurationLogEntry's shortcut of treating the previous latest configuration as committed sound. The truncation half is closed by geometry: the fallback lands on the committed configuration at index I, the truncation starts at the first conflicting index X, entries below X are identical to the leader's, and a committed configuration must be present in the log of the server that won afterwards, so X cannot be at or below I and that entry survives. I recorded the leader-gate Behaviour as reusable knowledge and noted the assumption the negative result rests on (a leader appending two uncommitted configurations, which this implementation prevents), along with counterevidence and the source-only nature of the account. No execution requested; the other four questions are unchanged.
